q1_issues.issue: "one of the most ... vehicles" is flattened to a plain generic (Inheritance language vehicle): the "one of the" partitive over a definite superset and the superlative ranking are both lost.

(Degree language systematic most) uses the superlative word as a Degree level, but the level slot is restricted to a lemmatized surface intensifier adverb or the three construction markers excessive/sufficient/insufficient, and superlatives route to (Most <scale> X <class>) instead.
Same unlicensed "most" level on (Degree language subtle most).
Same unlicensed "most" level on (Degree language significant most).

A spreading event is asserted at top level at (STV 1.0 0.99), but the sentence only says the vehicles are *for* spreading — no spreading is claimed to occur, so this asserts more than the text states.
(Instrument sk_spread_1 language) attaches a role to that unasserted event, and nothing anywhere records the "for"-relation between the vehicle claim and the spreading.

The three adjectives are attributive on "vehicles" inside the superlative NP, yet are predicated of language directly at generic strength, so the ranking-among-vehicles reading is replaced by three plain generics.

q2_gaps: "one of the most ADJ Ns" — a weakened/set-membership superlative combined with a cardinal partitive; neither the Most form nor the Partitives section covers the combination

a purpose/function "for V-ing" PP modifying a NOUN ("a vehicle for spreading X", "a tool for cutting") — the purpose-infinitive rule attaches (To <main-event> <purpose-event>) and presupposes a matrix event, which a noun-modifying gerund does not supply
coordination of three attributive adjectives under one superlative determiner ("the most A, B, and C Ns") — the scope of "most" over the coordination is unaddressed
notes: All heads used are licensed; the defects are structural (superlative-partitive flattened, function PP reified as an asserted event) plus an unlicensed value in the Degree level slot. Treating racist_ideology as a fused kind with its adjectival modifier genus exposed follows the compound rules correctly.
